AI Threads

My favorite way to build recently in Zed:
- Create a feature branch in git
- Describe feature to AI to generate the first pass
- Verify it works in browser
- Open branch diff in git panel (changes since main)
- Code review, line-by-line. Grill the output. Updates in the multi buffer happen live.
- Make test cases clearer, drop low-value tests
- When the code is exactly how I want it and easy to understand, open the PR
Cursor editor also has this branch diff!

Claude Code made it easy to build a SaaS product. It didn't make it any easier to build a SaaS company.
Building software used to be the moat. You had to raise money, hire a dev team, and spend a year shipping a v1. Now anyone can build, so people say the product no longer sets you apart and the moat moved to distribution. So go build a brand.
But distribution has always been a limiting factor, and the same AI tools that make it easier to build software also make it easier to market.

author: techmatician_official
text:
techmatician_official
Linux
09/17/26
Stop trying to learn the entire Linux OS before applying for IT jobs.
From working with Linux in real environments, the basics matter far more at entry level:
• Navigate the filesystem
• Find/edit files
• Understand chmod & chown
• Install packages
• Read logs
• SSH into a server
You don't need a dual-boot setup either.
Windows? Use WSL.
Mac? Open Terminal.
The goal is simple: when someone says “SSH into the server and check what’s wrong,” you shouldn't freeze.
Linux #SysAdmin #ITCareers
